task.name: An injected prior-run summary records what was selected but not how much prompt it consumed, so the size of the knowledge treatment is unknown
task.story_text:
An injected prior-run summary records what was selected but not how much prompt it consumed, so the size of the knowledge treatment is unknown

## Context

When prior-run context is injected, each included summary is recorded in the run's context manifest
with its source run, phase, rendering mode, the reasons it scored, its score and its admissibility
verdict. Nothing records how much of the prompt it occupied.

That quantity is the size of the treatment. Without it, several ordinary questions about the
knowledge loop have no answer from the records: how much context injection is displacing, whether a
summary that renders long is behaving differently from one that renders short, whether rendering
changes have made inclusions cheaper or more expensive over time, and what fraction of an assembled
prompt the corpus now occupies. Each of those is answerable per-run from the manifest if the size is
there, and answerable from nothing if it is not.

It is deliberately not a billing figure. A provider bills an invocation, not the individual pieces
of the prompt that went into it, and the all-in spend recorded against a run already contains
whatever the injected text cost. Recording a rendered size as though it were a cost invites it to
be subtracted from a total that already includes it, which would understate the price of injection
by counting it twice in opposite directions. The value of the figure is descriptive — how large the
treatment is — and it needs to be labelled in a way that keeps a later reader from spending it.

Counting also has to be interpretable later. A size measured under one tokenizer is not comparable
to a size measured under another, and rendering changes over time, so a bare number recorded today
becomes unreadable once either changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- A manifest entry recording an injected summary writes how much prompt that summary contributed,
  together with the identity of the method that produced the figure, so the number remains
  interpretable when the counting method or the rendering changes.
- The entry labels the figure as a rendered size, distinct from any billed or attributed cost. The
  report presents it as a size and never as spend, and derives no cost by subtracting it from a
  recorded invocation total.
- Where the size of an entry cannot be determined, the entry records that it is unavailable rather
  than writing a zero, so that an uncounted inclusion is never read as a weightless one.
- A run with no injected summaries writes no sizes, and the report returns none for it — distinct
  from a run whose injections were measured at zero.
- The report marks entries written before size capture existed as unmeasured rather than emitting
  them as inclusions of no size.
- The figure the entry writes describes the rendered summary alone, not the assembly that contained
  it, so summaries from different runs and phases remain comparable to each other.

## Example

A dev-phase manifest entry today:

```
- run_id: 27bb13e86070
  phase: dev
  rendering_mode: phase_summary
  score: 49
  reason: file_overlap(src/theforge/cli/shared.py), dir_overlap(tests), domain_match(cli), story_match
```

After this change the same entry also carries its size, and its provenance:

```
  rendered_size:
    value: 812
    unit: tokens
    method: cl100k_base
    kind: rendered_prompt_contribution   # descriptive, not billed spend
```

An entry whose size could not be counted records `value: null` with the reason, rather than `0`. A
run that received no summaries carries no `rendered_size` fields at all, rather than a set of zeros.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5-cli] Rendered prior-run summary sizes are recorded as descriptive manifest telemetry, legacy entries are marked unmeasured, and focused verification passed. | [anthropic-opus-cli] Rendered-size capture is wired correctly, but it counts via an undeclared optional dependency (tiktoken) that no supported install has, so every entry records value: null instead of a size.

findings.description: Rendered-size measurement is delegated to the tiktoken package, which is not listed in any dependency group in pyproject.toml and is not present in the repository venv, so exercising the helper in this checkout returns value None with unavailable_reason tiktoken_not_installed for every non-empty summary, meaning an injected summary's size is recorded as unavailable in every install rather than as a number.

The encoding lookup used to count a summary performs a first-use vocabulary fetch over the network when no local cache exists, and it runs inline on the context-assembly path for every selected candidate with no timeout, so a slow or blocked network stalls prompt assembly rather than degrading to an unavailable size.

No test asserts that a measured rendered size is an integer derived from the summary text; the available case is covered only by a hand-written fixture value in the audit-log test, while the selector tests assert unit, method, and kind or the unavailable payload.

finding_registry.description: Rendered-size measurement is delegated to the tiktoken package, which is not listed in any dependency group in pyproject.toml and is not present in the repository venv, so exercising the helper in this checkout returns value None with unavailable_reason tiktoken_not_installed for every non-empty summary, meaning an injected summary's size is recorded as unavailable in every install rather than as a number.

The encoding lookup used to count a summary performs a first-use vocabulary fetch over the network when no local cache exists, and it runs inline on the context-assembly path for every selected candidate with no timeout, so a slow or blocked network stalls prompt assembly rather than degrading to an unavailable size.

No test asserts that a measured rendered size is an integer derived from the summary text; the available case is covered only by a hand-written fixture value in the audit-log test, while the selector tests assert unit, method, and kind or the unavailable payload.

The reader migration that backfills pre-capture prior-run entries writes method cl100k_base into the rendered_size payload, while every entry the writer now produces carries method word_punctuation_estimate_v1, so a reader grouping recorded inclusions by counting method sees a cohort attributed to a tokenizer that no code in the project uses.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
